chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you approach the Black Stone, raise your hands, praise God, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Him to accept from you. Then touch the stone and kiss it. If you cannot kiss it, touch it with your hand; if you cannot touch it, gesture towards it and say: 'O God, I have delivered my trust and fulfilled my covenant, so that You may bear witness to my compliance. O God, as confirmation of Your Book and upon the Sunnah of Your Prophet, I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. I believed in God and disbelieved in al-Jibt and al-Taghut, and in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and in the worship of Satan and the worship of every rival called upon besides God. If you cannot say all of this, say part of it, and say: 'O God, to You I have extended my hand and in what is with You my desire has grown great, so accept my gift, forgive me, and have mercy on me. O God, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, and stations of disgrace in this world and the next.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions when touching the Black Stone during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual etiquette (adab) of Istilam, emphasizing the Black Stone as a tangible witness to the pilgrim's covenant with God. It prescribes a graduated hierarchy of physical contact—kissing, touching, or gesturing—accompanied by a comprehensive du'a that links the act to the Sunnah and affirms monotheism against pre-Islamic idols like Al-Lat and Al-Uzza. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on combining physical devotion with verbal testimony, reinforcing the Stone's role as a symbol of fidelity to the divine promise.
